subject: Geopolitics
title: Assassination Programs
description: A micro-lesson that makes Assassination Programs usable.

hook.text: Israel's Mossad hunted every organizer of the Munich Olympics massacre. It took years, but it found them all.

buildup.text: Targeted killings are the sharpest tool of covert action. Nations use them to eliminate threats without declared war.

discovery.text: The US drone program killed thousands of suspected terrorists. The legal framework remains contested globally.

twist.text: Russia poisoned dissidents on foreign soil. Saudi Arabia murdered Khashoggi in a consulate. Norms are eroding fast.

climax.text: Assassinations remove individuals but rarely remove movements. New leaders emerge, often more radical than the last.

punchline.text: You can kill a leader but not an idea.

quiz.question: Why are targeted killings often considered strategically limited?
options: They are too expensive to conduct regularly
They remove individuals but not movements; new leaders emerge
